# Whether every member of a ball is positive, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_positive_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $0 < x$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty, $X$ the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$; a mask that is true only if it holds:

$$m \implies X \ne \emptyset \text{ and } 0 < x \text{ for every } x \in X.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.certainly_positive()` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `bool` | `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c$ and radius $r$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $m$ is true exactly when $0 < x$ for every $x \in X$, $X$ not being empty: the answer is exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_positive_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_positive_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_positive_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius compared with the center (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_positive_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_positive_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# Whether every member of a ball with a one-limb center is positive, and the ball is not empty
# (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", the row of certainly_positive()): c - r > 0, decided
# exactly as r < c. False for the empty set (a NaN compares false) and for the whole line (+inf < 0
# is false). The comparison of Ball<T, 1>::certainly_positive, written by hand in
# include/kairn/ball.hpp. Exact.

m = lt(r, c)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
